question_en: Do I have to pay to get Udyam registration for my homestay or craft work?
answer: No. Udyam registration is free and done online by self-declaration. The official portal says no fee is to be paid to anyone. Any website or agent that asks for money is not the official portal.
actions: Open only udyamregistration.gov.in on the phone or ask a Common Service Centre (CSC) operator to help.
Keep your Aadhaar number and PAN ready.
Refuse any person or site that asks for a registration fee.
caution: Many fake sites copy the Udyam name. The portal itself warns about this.
evidence: Udyam portal home page and PIB release of 14 July 2026, both read on 2 Oct 2026: registration is free, paperless, self-declaration based.
verify_with: Udyam portal helpline or District Industries Centre (DIC)

question_en: What do I get if I register on Udyam? Is it worth it for a small village enterprise?
answer: Udyam gives your enterprise an official identity. PIB lists these benefits: easier access to bank credit and government schemes, eligibility for government buying, a portal for delayed-payment disputes, and a chance to join trade exhibitions. It does not by itself give you money. Each scheme still has its own rules.
actions: Register on Udyam before you apply for MUDRA, CGTMSE-backed loans or other MSME schemes.
Ask your bank which schemes need an Udyam number.
Keep a printout or PDF of the certificate in your records.
caution: Do not pay anyone to 'guarantee' benefits.
context_needed: whether the enterprise is an individual, group or company
evidence: PIB release 14 July 2026 lists benefits: credit access, schemes, procurement, MSME Online Dispute Resolution portal, exhibitions.

question_en: I do not have a GST number. Can I still register on Udyam?
answer: The official sources do not fully agree, so ask before you rely on either. The Udyam home page says PAN and GSTIN are needed 'as per applicability' under the GST law. A PIB release of July 2026 says GST registration is not required, and that the Udyam Assist Platform is for informal micro enterprises that may not have GST. Informal enterprises can register through partners such as banks.
actions: Ask a bank, DIC or CSC whether your activity needs GST at all.
If you have no GST, ask them about the Udyam Assist Platform.
Check the Udyam portal again before you apply because rules are being updated.
caution: A 2026 MSME amendment Bill was introduced in Parliament in August 2026. Its final status was not confirmed. Rules may change.
context_needed: whether you sell goods or services
evidence: Udyam home page (GSTIN as per applicability) vs PIB 14 July 2026 (GST not required; Udyam Assist Platform). Conflict noted.

question_en: Is my small homestay a 'micro' enterprise? What is the size limit?
answer: On the Udyam portal, a micro enterprise has investment up to Rs 2.5 crore and turnover up to Rs 10 crore (limits applying from 1 April 2025). Almost every village homestay or craft group is far below this. The portal also lists small and medium limits for larger businesses.
actions: Use your actual investment and yearly sales when you register.
Re-check the limits on udyamregistration.gov.in each year.
caution: Limits can be revised by the government.
evidence: Udyam portal home page, as of April 2025 limits, read 2 Oct 2026.

question_en: Our village wants to run tourism together. Should we form an SHG, a cooperative, a society or a company?
answer: It depends on what you want to do. SHG: easy to start, good for small savings and loans among members, mostly women. Cooperative: members own it and share profit by use; rules differ by state. Society or trust: good for community or charity work, not for sharing profit. Section 8 company: a non-profit company with more paperwork. FPO or producer company: for farmers selling or processing produce. A committee under the Gram Panchayat has no automatic legal power to sign contracts or hold money.
actions: List what you want to do together: run homestays, sell crafts, share income, take a loan.
Take the list to the Block office, DAY-NRLM block mission or a lawyer or Chartered Accountant before choosing.
Write down who owns the group and how profit is shared before you register.
caution: This is general guidance, not legal advice. Registration rules, fees and tax treatment differ by state and law. Confirm with the Registrar or a qualified adviser.
evidence: Method answer based on general practice. FPO definition in S167 is used only for the FPO line.
verify_with: Registrar of Cooperative Societies, Registrar of Societies, ROC, or a Chartered Accountant

question_en: Can our women's SHG start a tourism activity like cooking for guests or selling crafts?
answer: Yes, an SHG can take up income activities with its members. SHGs under DAY-NRLM can get a Revolving Fund and a Community Investment Fund, and can take bank credit with interest subvention. Before you start, check food, hygiene and local permission rules for the activity you choose. Keep the group's money in the group bank account.
actions: Talk to your Village Organisation or Block Mission Manager of DAY-NRLM about your plan.
Write a one-page plan: who does what, what it costs, who buys.
Start with one small activity and test it for a season.
caution: Loans must be repaid from real income. Do not take a loan before you have tested demand.
context_needed: whether the SHG is under DAY-NRLM
evidence: PIB release on bank credit to women SHGs: Revolving Fund, Community Investment Fund, interest subvention, SVEP.
verify_with: Block Mission Manager, DAY-NRLM / State Rural Livelihoods Mission

question_en: We are farmers in a Farmer Producer Organisation. Can our FPO also run farm visits or sell products to guests?
answer: An FPO is a farmers' organisation registered under Part IXA of the Companies Act or under a Cooperative Societies Act. What it may do depends on the 'objects' written in its registration papers. Farm visits may not be covered. Ask your FPO's board, the promoting agency (CBBO) and the person who handles its legal filings whether the objects allow tourism work.
actions: Read the objects clause in your FPO's registration papers.
Ask your Board and legal adviser if an amendment is needed.
Start with selling produce and processed goods to visitors, which is closer to normal FPO work.
caution: Do not start new activity with FPO funds without a board decision and legal advice.
evidence: PIB release (Feb 2025) defines FPO and lists its support. The question of tourism objects is a method point, not a rule read.
verify_with: FPO's promoting agency / ROC or Registrar of Cooperative Societies / lawyer

question_en: Is a cooperative society better than a trust for sharing income among homestay families?
answer: A cooperative is owned by its members and is set up so members benefit from the group's business. A trust or a society is usually for community or charitable purposes. How profit can be shared depends on the law and your papers. Cooperative laws are made by states, so rules and forms differ.
actions: Meet the Registrar of Cooperative Societies or the Assistant Registrar at your district office.
Ask which model fits a group of households that each run their own homestay.
Get the model bye-laws in your language before you draft your own.
caution: I could not verify state cooperative rules in this session. Treat this as general guidance only.
context_needed: whether income is shared or each family earns separately
evidence: General practice answer. State cooperative laws were not read.
verify_with: District Registrar of Cooperative Societies / Chartered Accountant

question_en: Can the Gram Panchayat form a village tourism committee? Can the committee open a bank account?
answer: Many villages use a committee with homestay owners, women, youth and the Sarpanch. A committee made by a Gram Panchayat resolution is mainly a decision and coordination group. Whether it can hold a bank account or sign contracts depends on how it is registered and on state rules. The safe way is to register the group as a society, cooperative or similar body.
actions: Hold a Gram Sabha meeting and record the decision to form the committee.
Ask the Block Development Office or Panchayat Secretary if your state allows the committee to open an account.
Do not keep tourism money in one person's personal account.
caution: State Panchayati Raj rules differ. This answer is a method, not a rule from any state.
evidence: General practice. No state Panchayati Raj rule was read.

question_en: When do I have to take a GST number? We earn only a little from guests.
answer: Under Section 22 of the CGST Act, a supplier must register if yearly turnover is more than Rs 20 lakh. In special category states the limit is Rs 10 lakh. For businesses that supply only goods, the limit can be higher, up to Rs 40 lakh, if the state is notified. Turnover counts all supplies, not only profit. GST rates and exemptions on stays and services were revised in 2025 and were not checked here.
actions: Add up your total yearly receipts from guests and sales.
Ask a Chartered Accountant or the GST helpdesk if your activity is exempt or taxable.
Register on gst.gov.in if you cross the limit or if a buyer or platform requires it.
caution: This is not tax advice. Interstate sales and online platform sales can need GST even below the limit. Verify with a tax professional.
evidence: CGST Act Section 22 on CBIC tax repository, read 2 Oct 2026.
verify_with: Chartered Accountant / GST helpdesk / GST officer

question_en: Whose name should the bank account be in for our group's tourism income?
answer: Open the account in the name of the group, such as the SHG, society or cooperative, with two or three authorised signatories. Do not use one person's personal account for group money. This keeps income clear and protects you if there is a dispute or illness.
actions: Ask the bank which papers a group account needs for your type of group.
Choose signatories from different families, and include at least one woman.
Deposit all guest payments into this account and issue a receipt for each one.
caution: Bank rules (KYC) differ by bank. Ask your bank branch.
evidence: General practice.
verify_with: Bank branch manager / Lead District Manager

question_en: How can our village share tourism income fairly between families?
answer: Agree the rules in a village meeting before the first guest arrives. A common method is to split money into three parts: the host or worker who did the service, a small village fund for shared needs, and a reserve for repairs and slow months. Decide the percentages together and write them down. Do not copy another village's numbers without discussing.
actions: Hold a meeting with women, youth, elders and all involved families.
Write the sharing rule in simple words and read it aloud.
Review the rule after one season and change it if needed.
caution: Sharing models can create fights if rules are vague. Use a neutral person to keep the register.
evidence: Practice-based method. No percentages are given on purpose.
verify_with: A trusted local NGO or the Block Mission Manager can help facilitate

question_en: What records should our collective keep so nobody doubts the money?
answer: Keep four simple records: a cash book (money in and out), a receipt book, a guest or booking register, and meeting minutes. Read the monthly summary aloud at the group meeting. Two people should check it. Keep bank statements and bills in one file.
actions: Start a cash book from the first day and write every payment.
Give a numbered receipt for every guest payment.
Show the month's accounts at the group meeting and get signatures.
caution: If you cross GST or income tax limits, you may need more records. Ask a Chartered Accountant.
evidence: Practice-based method.

question_en: Which loan can I take to add two rooms to my homestay?
answer: There is no single loan only for homestay rooms. Ask your bank about a MUDRA loan or a normal term loan. MUDRA loans go to non-corporate, non-farm small and micro enterprises. PMEGP gives a subsidy for new non-farm micro projects. In tribal areas, a homestay grant was announced, but check if funds are released. Bank rules decide, so ask at the branch and the DIC.
actions: Write the cost of two rooms and your expected guests for the year.
Visit your bank and the District Industries Centre with the plan and your Udyam number.
Ask what collateral, margin money and repayment time the bank requires.
caution: Borrow only what you can repay if guests are fewer than you expect. Do not use informal moneylenders.
evidence: MUDRA home page, MUDRA limits PDF, PMEGP release, rural tourism release read 2 Oct 2026. Eligibility of homestay rooms for each scheme was not confirmed.

question_en: What are the MUDRA loan categories and how much can I get?
answer: As officially stated: Shishu is up to Rs 50,000. Kishore is above Rs 50,000 up to Rs 5 lakh. Tarun is above Rs 5 lakh up to Rs 10 lakh. Tarun Plus is above Rs 10 lakh up to Rs 20 lakh, only for people who took and repaid a Tarun loan. Tarun Plus took effect on 24 October 2024. The bank still decides your loan after checking your plan.
actions: Choose the category that matches your cost, starting small.
Take your Aadhaar, PAN, bank passbook and a short business plan to the bank.
Ask the bank to confirm current limits and interest rate.
caution: Limits can change. Verify on mudra.org.in or with a bank.
evidence: PIB document on Tarun Plus (effective 24 Oct 2024) and MUDRA home page.

question_en: A person says he can get my MUDRA loan sanctioned if I give him some money. Is that right?
answer: No. The MUDRA website says MUDRA has no agents or middlemen. You can apply at a bank branch or online at udyamimitra.in. Paying a person to get a loan is a warning sign of cheating.
actions: Do not pay anyone before the bank sanctions the loan.
Apply directly at the branch or on udyamimitra.in.
Report cheating to the bank manager and to cybercrime helpline 1930 if money was sent online.
caution: Keep any messages or payment proof. Never share OTP or PIN.
evidence: MUDRA home page: no agents; apply at branch or udyamimitra.in. PIB cyber fraud release: helpline 1930.

question_en: The bank asks for security. What is CGTMSE and can it help me avoid giving collateral?
answer: CGTMSE does not give loans. It guarantees credit given by member banks and some other lenders to micro and small enterprises. The scheme provides collateral-free and third-party-guarantee-free credit facilities. The maximum guarantee cover is now Rs 10 crore. Your bank applies for the cover, not you. The CGTMSE site says it has no agents.
actions: Ask your bank manager if the loan can be covered under CGTMSE.
Have your Udyam registration and project papers ready.
Do not pay any agent for the cover.
caution: The bank decides whether to lend. A guarantee does not mean automatic approval.
evidence: CGTMSE home page read 2 Oct 2026.

question_en: I am an SC/ST or a woman entrepreneur. Is Stand-Up India loan useful for starting a homestay?
answer: Stand-Up India is for SC, ST and women entrepreneurs starting a new (greenfield) enterprise in manufacturing, services, trading or agriculture-allied activities. Bank loans are Rs 10 lakh to Rs 1 crore. At least one SC/ST borrower and one woman borrower per bank branch are targeted. You can apply on standupmitra.in.  Whether a homestay qualifies as a 'service' is for the bank to decide.
actions: Check on standupmitra.in if the scheme is currently open for new applications.
Prepare a project report with costs and expected guests.
Visit the bank branch with the report.
caution: An older PIB note said the scheme was extended up to 2025. I could not confirm validity after that. The loan range is big, so do not borrow more than you can repay.
evidence: PIB (2025) says Rs 10 lakh to Rs 1 crore.

question_en: Is there a government subsidy for starting a new small business like a craft unit or food unit?
answer: PMEGP gives a subsidy on the project cost for new non-farm micro enterprises. For the 2021-22 to 2025-26 period, rural subsidy was 35 percent for special categories (SC, ST, OBC, women and others listed) and 25 percent for general. Maximum project cost was Rs 50 lakh for manufacturing and Rs 20 lakh for service. Apply online on the KVIC portal. Whether PMEGP is running after March 2026 was not confirmed.
actions: Ask the District Industries Centre or KVIC office if PMEGP is open now.
Check if your activity (craft, food unit, service) is allowed.
Prepare a project report and talk to the bank first.
caution: Existing units and some earlier scheme beneficiaries may not qualify. Confirm the rules in the current guidelines.
evidence: PIB release on PMEGP continuation 2021-22 to 2025-26.

question_en: What money support can our SHG get from DAY-NRLM?
answer: A PIB release (data to Nov 2024) says DAY-NRLM gives Revolving Funds of Rs 20,000 to 30,000 per SHG and Community Investment Funds up to Rs 2.5 lakh per SHG. SHGs can also take bank loans with interest subvention. Older papers mention Rs 15,000 for the revolving fund, so amounts may differ by state or period. Your Block Mission Manager can tell you what applies to your SHG.
actions: Ask the Community Resource Person or Block office if your SHG has taken RF and CIF.
Keep SHG books and bank statements updated.
Ask about interest subvention before taking a bank loan.
caution: Funds go to SHGs under the Mission, usually after grading. Check eligibility locally.
evidence: PIB release on bank credit to women SHGs.
verify_with: Block Mission Manager / State Rural Livelihoods Mission

question_en: What is SVEP? Can it help me start a small business in my village?
answer: SVEP is a part of DAY-NRLM for non-farm businesses in villages. It gives training, mentoring and credit help. A trained Community Resource Person (CRP-EP) supports up to 50 enterprises. The scheme can give Community Enterprise Fund loans. It runs in selected blocks, so your block may not have it.
actions: Ask the Block Mission Manager if SVEP is running in your block.
If yes, meet the CRP-EP and share your business idea.
If no, ask about other DAY-NRLM support.
caution: The loan size and terms were not stated in the release I read. Ask the Block office.
evidence: PIB backgrounder on SVEP dated 25 July 2026.

question_en: I am a potter, basket maker or tailor. Can I get help from PM Vishwakarma?
answer: PM Vishwakarma covers 18 traditional trades, for example carpenter, potter, mason, tailor, basket/mat/broom maker, doll and toy maker, garland maker and others. The Cabinet note lists a certificate and ID card, credit support of Rs 1 lakh then Rs 2 lakh at 5 percent, skill training, toolkit incentive, digital incentive and marketing support. A secondary source adds: age above 18, self-employed, one person per family, and no government employees. The scheme period runs to 2027-28.
actions: Check if your trade is on the 18-trade list at pmvishwakarma.gov.in.
Go to a Common Service Centre or Gram Panchayat office to register.
Ask about training and toolkit dates after registration.
caution: Details such as stipend and toolkit amounts come from a secondary source. Confirm on the official portal.
evidence: PIB Cabinet release (trades, credit, period) read; eligibility and toolkit amounts from a secondary source.

question_en: Our women's group makes pickle and jam. Can we get a subsidy to set up the unit?
answer: PMFME supports micro food processing units. Individual units get a 35 percent credit-linked subsidy up to Rs 10 lakh per unit. SHG members get seed capital of Rs 40,000 per member for working capital and small tools. Common facilities can get 35 percent subsidy. A 2026 release says the scheme was extended till September 2026, so it may have ended by now. Ask your State Nodal Agency.
actions: Ask the District Resource Person under PMFME or the DIC if the scheme is still taking applications.
Get FSSAI registration or licence as your food agent advises.
Prepare a simple project plan with costs and market.
caution: Scheme status after September 2026 is unconfirmed. Food safety rules apply separately.
evidence: Two PIB releases (Dec 2025 and 2026) read.
verify_with: State Nodal Agency for PMFME / DIC

question_en: I live in a tribal area. Can I get a grant to build or repair a homestay?
answer: A tribal homestay support was announced under Swadesh Darshan and PM-JUGA. The Ministry says up to Rs 5 lakh per unit for new building, up to Rs 3 lakh for repair, and Rs 5 lakh for village community needs, with a target of 1,000 homestays. In August 2025 the Ministry said no funds had been released. Please check the current status with your State Tourism Department.
actions: Ask the District Tourism Officer or Tribal Welfare office if the scheme is open in your area.
Keep land and ownership papers and ID ready.
Register your homestay as per your state's homestay rules.
caution: The scheme was at draft guideline stage in 2025. Do not borrow money expecting this grant.
evidence: PIB (Jan 2026) lists amounts; Lok Sabha reply (Aug 2025) says no funds released.
verify_with: State Tourism Department / Tribal Welfare Department

question_en: Does my state give any subsidy or help to homestay owners?
answer: Many states run their own homestay or rural tourism schemes, but rules and amounts differ and change. The Ministry of Tourism says state governments lead tourism development. Use the stay agent for your state's registration. For money support, ask your District Tourism Office for current schemes.
actions: Call or visit the District Tourism Office and ask about homestay registration and any support.
Check your state tourism website for the latest scheme guidelines.
Keep your registration certificate ready for bank and scheme applications.
caution: Do not rely on old news or social media posts about subsidies. Confirm in writing.
evidence: PIB Jan 2026: states lead tourism development. No state scheme was read.
verify_with: District Tourism Officer / State Tourism Department

question_en: Can NABARD help us with money for village tourism or farm-based activities?
answer: NABARD mostly works through banks and institutions, not by lending directly to a family. Its district officer (DDM) can tell you what is running in your district for SHGs, farmer groups and rural enterprises. I could not confirm a NABARD scheme made only for rural tourism or agri-tourism. Ask your bank and the District Development Manager.
actions: Ask the Lead District Manager (LDM) or NABARD DDM which schemes support farm and non-farm enterprises.
Show your plan and group papers.
Ask if a grant or training is available for your type of group.
caution: NABARD pages could not be read in this session. Treat this as a referral.
evidence: NABARD website could not be read. General pointer.
verify_with: NABARD District Development Manager / Lead District Manager

question_en: How can our village get CSR or NGO funding for tourism training or facilities?
answer: Companies that spend CSR money usually fund projects through registered non-profits or their own foundations. Contact the NGO or Foundation working in your area, or the company's CSR office near you. Prepare a short proposal: the need, what you will do, cost, who benefits, and how you will report. Show that your village agrees.
actions: Write a 2-page proposal with a budget and a list of beneficiaries.
Ask a registered NGO or your Block office to partner if you are not registered.
Keep accounts and photos with consent to report back.
caution: Funders have their own conditions. Never pay a fee to anyone who promises to get you a grant.
evidence: Practice-based. CSR rules were not read in this session.

question_en: Can we raise money online from well-wishers or guests to rebuild our guest house?
answer: It can work, but be careful. Be clear about what the money is for, who holds it and how you will report. Use a group account or registered body, not one person's account. Keep proof of every spend. Rules for donations and tax can differ by organisation type.
actions: Write the purpose and total amount in simple words before you ask.
Ask a Chartered Accountant or a legal adviser about rules for your kind of group.
Share updates and bills with donors.
caution: Beware of fake donation pages and of foreign donations, which can need special permission. Confirm with a qualified adviser.
evidence: Practice-based. Foreign donation (FCRA) rules not read.

question_en: I am new to tourism. How much should I borrow to start?
answer: Borrow as little as possible at first. Test with a few guests using what you have. Then add only what guests ask for. Do not borrow from informal moneylenders. Use banks, SHG funds or recognised lenders. Check that your monthly repayment is lower than what you can earn in slow months.
actions: Run a trial season with existing rooms or meals before taking a loan.
Write what you will earn in good and slow months, then choose a loan you can pay in the slow months.
Take written loan terms and ask the bank to explain interest and fees.
caution: Never sign blank papers. Never give your Aadhaar, PAN or bank PIN to loan agents.
evidence: Practice-based. MUDRA site notes no agents are used.

question_en: Is there an official certificate course for homestay hosts?
answer: Yes. The Tourism & Hospitality Skill Council (THSC) has a qualification called Home Stay Host (NSQF level 4.5). It trains you to prepare the home, host guests, communicate well, protect guest privacy, keep health, hygiene and safety, and use employability skills. The qualification file lists a minimum age of 18 and certain education and experience entry options. Training is run by approved training partners.
actions: Ask a THSC training partner or your District Skill Committee if a Home Stay Host batch is running near you.
Check the entry requirements for your education and experience.
Ask if Recognition of Prior Learning is available if you already host guests.
caution: Course hours, fees and batches were not confirmed. This certificate is not the same as your state's homestay registration.
evidence: THSC qualification file for Home Stay Host read 2 Oct 2026.

question_en: Is there a certificate for village cooks, housekeeping or guide work?
answer: Yes, THSC and NSDC list qualification packs for hospitality roles such as housekeeping, kitchen helpers and guest-house roles. Check the exact job-role names and levels on thsc.in or the NSDC Skill India Digital portal, or ask a training partner. I could not confirm a specific cook or guide qualification title in this session.
actions: Visit thsc.in or call a THSC training partner and ask for the list of job roles for your work.
Ask which roles can be certified through Recognition of Prior Learning.
Match the job role to what you already do.
caution: Do not pay anyone who is not an approved training partner.
evidence: General pointer. THSC job role listing could not be read in full.
verify_with: THSC / NSDC / Skill India Digital portal

question_en: I want to become a certified local guide or tourist facilitator. What does the Ministry of Tourism offer?
answer: The Ministry of Tourism runs the Incredible India Tourist Facilitator (IITF) online programme with a basic course, advanced heritage and adventure courses, spoken language training and refresher courses. A 2025 reply in Parliament says SC and ST candidates get a fee exemption. Check the portal for the current fee, eligibility and how to register.
actions: Search for the Incredible India Tourist Facilitator portal on the Ministry of Tourism website.
Check eligibility and fee for the course you want.
Ask your District Tourism Office about regional guide licensing in your state.
caution: IITF is a certificate course. Rules for licensed guides at monuments and parks differ by state or agency.
evidence: Ministry of Tourism Lok Sabha reply of 18 Aug 2025.
verify_with: Ministry of Tourism / District Tourism Office

question_en: Is the Hunar Se Rozgar Tak tourism training still running?
answer: I could not verify the current status of Hunar Se Rozgar Tak. The 2025 Ministry of Tourism reply I read did not mention it. Ask your District Tourism Office or the nearest Institute of Hotel Management or Food Craft Institute if free tourism and hospitality training batches are running.
actions: Call the District Tourism Office and ask for current free training.
Ask the nearest IHM or Food Craft Institute.
Check Skill India Digital for free hospitality courses.
caution: Do not pay for any scheme-based free training.
evidence: Not confirmed. Written as a referral.
verify_with: District Tourism Office / Ministry of Tourism

question_en: Is there free skill training under the government for my son or daughter in hospitality?
answer: PMKVY 4.0 guidelines say Short Term Training is free for Indian nationals aged 15 to 45 with Aadhaar, mostly for school or college dropouts and unemployed youth. Learners get an induction kit. There is no money paid to the candidate as per the guidelines. Courses and centres differ by area, so ask your nearest PMKVY or Skill India centre.
actions: Find the nearest Skill India Centre or ask the District Skill Committee.
Carry Aadhaar and bank details.
Ask which hospitality or tourism job roles are being offered.
caution: Guidelines are from February 2024. Check current batches locally.
evidence: PMKVY 4.0 guidelines PDF read.
verify_with: Skill India Centre / District Skill Committee

question_en: I have cooked for guests for years but have no certificate. Can I get certified?
answer: Yes, Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) is for people who already have work experience. Under PMKVY 4.0 guidelines, candidates are 18 to 59 years old and have experience in the job role. They are screened first, then take bridge training of 30 to 132 hours, then a final assessment and certification. A job role must exist for your work.
actions: Ask a Skill India or THSC training partner if there is an RPL batch for your job role.
Collect proof of experience such as photos, guest letters or a letter from the Panchayat.
Attend the assessment on the given date.
caution: RPL availability depends on local projects. Confirm batch and fees locally.
evidence: PMKVY 4.0 guidelines PDF read.
verify_with: Skill India Centre / sector skill council

question_en: Where can rural youth get free training to start their own small business?
answer: Rural Self Employment Training Institutes (RSETIs) are run by banks. They train rural poor youth, including BPL youth, for self-employment. A PIB note says 64 approved vocational programmes are offered. Age, fees and food or lodging terms were not in the page I read. Ask the nearest RSETI of your district's lead bank.
actions: Ask the Lead District Manager for the nearest RSETI.
Ask which programmes are open and what is required to join.
Ask about help with loans after the training.
caution: Eligibility and course lists change. Verify at the RSETI.
evidence: PIB release on RSETI read 2 Oct 2026.
verify_with: RSETI of your district / Lead District Manager

question_en: Our village wants to start farm visits. Can the Krishi Vigyan Kendra help us?
answer: KVKs are district-level farm centres under ICAR. They train farmers, women and youth, give farm advice, test soil, hold demonstrations and supply seeds and planting material. A KVK can help you improve what guests will see on the farm, such as crops, kitchen gardens and processing. Ask if they also support value-added products.
actions: Visit or call your district KVK and ask for the training calendar.
Ask for help with crop planning and safe use of farm inputs near guests.
Invite the KVK scientist to visit before your first guest group.
caution: KVKs may not train on tourism itself. Use them for farm skills.
evidence: ICAR page on KVKs read 2 Oct 2026.

question_en: Where in the village can I get help to make a profile, take digital payments or register for schemes?
answer: Common Service Centres (CSCs) run by Village Level Entrepreneurs (VLEs) help with online government services and other digital work. Some government scheme registrations are also done through CSCs; ask the VLE. Ask the VLE about digital literacy classes and about help with online forms. Services and charges differ.
actions: Find your nearest CSC at the Digital Seva portal or ask the Gram Panchayat.
Ask which services and fees apply before you give documents.
Keep a copy of every form you submit.
caution: Never share OTPs or bank PINs with a VLE or anyone else.
evidence: General practice. CSC page read but not listed as a source.

question_en: Can I learn hospitality skills online for free on my phone?
answer: Official free options exist but change. Check the Skill India Digital portal for free hospitality and tourism courses, and the Ministry of Tourism's IITF online platform. A YouTube lesson alone does not give a recognised certificate. I did not read the course lists in this session.
actions: Search for Skill India Digital Hub on your phone and make a login.
Filter for hospitality or tourism.
Ask your trainer or CSC for help with the first login.
caution: Use only official portals. Do not pay for a 'government certificate'.
evidence: Not verified. Referral only.

question_en: How do I get an artisan card and what does it give me?
answer: The Pehchan card is an Aadhaar-linked identity card for handicraft artisans, issued after field verification by officials of the Development Commissioner (Handicrafts). A PIB note says cardholders can access training, design workshops, toolkits, marketing support and MUDRA loans with interest subvention. Ask your nearest Handicrafts office or Weavers' Service Centre how to apply.
actions: Keep Aadhaar and a few examples of your craft ready.
Contact the nearest Handicrafts Service Centre or check handicrafts.nic.in.
After the card, ask about marketing events and training.
caution: Benefits depend on scheme rules and funds. Check what is open now.
evidence: PIB release on PEHCHAN read, data as of June 2023.

question_en: What are Craftmark and Handloom Mark, and should I use them?
answer: Craftmark and Handloom Mark are government-linked marks that help buyers recognise genuine handmade or handloom goods. I could not verify how to apply or any fee in this session. Ask the Development Commissioner (Handicrafts) or the Weavers' Service Centre for the current process. You can still use honest labels with your own name and story.
actions: Ask the Handicrafts Service Centre or Weavers' Service Centre about the process.
Meanwhile, put a simple label with maker name, place and material on every product.
Do not print a mark on products unless you are registered for it.
caution: Using a mark without registration may cause legal problems.
evidence: Not verified in detail. Referral only.

question_en: Can I sell my handmade products online through a government site?
answer: Indiahandmade is a digital marketplace for handloom weavers, handicraft artisans and producer organisations, run with the Ministry of Textiles. PIB says small sellers without GST can register with an Enrolment ID but can sell only within their own state. The platform offers guided onboarding and shows GI-tagged and ODOP items.
actions: Keep your Pehchan card or weaver ID, Aadhaar and bank details ready.
Ask your Weavers' Service Centre or CSC about onboarding.
Take clear photos and write simple product descriptions.
caution: Platform fees and terms were not stated in the release. Read them before you sign.
evidence: PIB document 6 July 2026 read.

question_en: Our product has a GI tag. Can I use it on my products? How does our group get GI?
answer: A GI protects a product linked to a place. Any association of producers, organisation or authority can apply for a GI. A producer can register as an authorised user of a registered GI by a written application with the fee. Registration lasts 10 years and can be renewed. Only authorised users get the exclusive right to use the GI for those goods. Do not print the GI on your product until you are registered.
actions: Check if your product's GI is registered and who the registered proprietor is.
Ask the GI proprietor or a support agency how to become an authorised user.
If no GI exists, form a producer group and ask a GI facilitation agency about applying.
caution: Applications go to the GI Registry in Chennai, often through a registered agent. Fees were not stated in the page I read.
evidence: IP India GI FAQ read 2 Oct 2026.
verify_with: GI Registry / state GI support cell

question_en: What is ODOP and can my village product get support?
answer: ODOP picks one special product per district, selected by states. Products on the list may get priority in some support schemes. For example, PMFME gives priority to ODOP products for SHG seed capital. Ask your District Industries Centre which product is listed for your district and what support is open.
actions: Find your district's ODOP product from the DIC.
If your product matches, mention ODOP in your applications.
If not, ask about other schemes.
caution: Support differs by state and scheme.
evidence: PMFME PIB releases mention ODOP priority. The ODOP page itself was read but is not listed.

question_en: Can our women's group sell to government offices through GeM?
answer: Yes, women-led micro and small enterprises and SHGs can sell on GeM through the Womaniya initiative, for example handicrafts, handloom and groceries. Registration uses Udyam verification and documents. GeM runs training workshops for sellers. Buyers are government departments, so this is not for selling to individual tourists.
actions: Get Udyam registration for your group or enterprise.
Ask the GeM helpdesk or a CSC to assist with seller registration.
Check product categories and prices in similar listings.
caution: Fees and rules were not stated in the release. Check the GeM portal.
evidence: PIB release on Womaniya read.

question_en: What is ONDC and how can a small village seller join?
answer: ONDC is an open network, not a shop. Sellers join through ONDC-compliant seller apps. The Ministry of MSME TEAM scheme offers financial help for onboarding, cataloguing and logistics. SIDBI and NABARD support SHGs and social sector sellers. eSaras lists SHG handicrafts.
actions: Ask a CSC or seller app helper to onboard you.
Prepare photos, product descriptions and product weights.
Check platform fees and delivery terms before you sign.
caution: Compare more than one seller app. Never share OTPs.
evidence: PIB release of 22 July 2025 read.
verify_with: CSC / seller app support / MSME DFO

question_en: We are a tribal community making forest products and crafts. Who can buy from us?
answer: Tribes India is the retail arm of TRIFED under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs. It sources from tribal artisans and groups. Van Dhan Vikas Kendras help tribal gatherers form groups. I could not confirm how to join in this session. Ask the Tribal Welfare Department, the nearest TRIFED regional office or your ITDA/ITDP office.
actions: Contact the Tribal Welfare Department or ITDA office.
Ask TRIFED's regional office about empanelment of artisans and groups.
Keep proof of tribal identity and group papers.
caution: Terms of supply and prices are agreed with the buyer. Read them before signing.
evidence: TRIFED PIB release was read but is not listed as a source. Referral only.
verify_with: TRIFED regional office / Tribal Welfare Department

question_en: How can our SHG get a stall at exhibitions like SARAS Aajeevika Mela?
answer: SARAS fairs showcase products of SHG women under DAY-NRLM, and eSARAS (www.esaras.in) is its online marketplace. Stall selection is usually coordinated through the state rural livelihoods mission. For artisans, Dilli Haat and other events are coordinated by the Development Commissioner (Handicrafts), where artisans apply with the Pehchan card. Ask your Block Mission Manager or Handicrafts office for the next dates.
actions: Ask the Block Mission Manager about the next SARAS or state fair.
Keep product samples, price list and stock ready.
If you are an artisan, check if your Pehchan card is active.
caution: Selection and fees differ by event. Confirm in writing.
evidence: eSARAS named in PIB release on SHG credit. Selection details not verified.

question_en: How do we sell our crafts to guests honestly and fairly?
answer: Tell the truth about each item: who made it, where, from what material, and how long it took. Put a small tag with the maker's name or group, village and care tips. Do not call a machine-made item handmade. Let guests buy without pressure. Pay the maker the agreed price on time and record each sale.
actions: Make a tag for each product with maker name, village, material and one line about the craft.
Agree a fixed fair price with each maker before items go on display.
Keep a sales register and pay makers on the day or as agreed.
caution: Do not copy another community's designs or use sacred symbols without permission. Use GI or other marks only if you are authorised.
evidence: Practice-based.

question_en: How do I fix a fair price for my handmade product without guessing?
answer: Add up four things: cost of materials, your working time at a fair daily wage, a share for tools and space, and a small amount for risk and savings. Compare with similar items in nearby markets, but do not copy a price that does not cover your time. Check the price with a few buyers and adjust slowly.
actions: Note materials, hours worked and other costs for one piece.
Value your time at a fair day rate and add it.
Test the price with two or three guests and revise if needed.
caution: Selling too low harms all makers in the village. Agree price rules in your group.
evidence: Practice-based method. No price numbers.

question_en: Can our women's group sell pickle and snacks to guests?
answer: Selling packed food to guests is a food business. Food safety rules apply, such as FSSAI registration or licence depending on the size of your work. The food safety agent can tell you what applies. PMFME can support micro food processing units, and SHG members can get seed capital under PMFME if the scheme is open.
actions: Ask your District Food Safety Officer what registration your food unit needs.
Use clean containers, clear labels and a batch date.
Ask the DIC if PMFME support is open.
caution: Do not sell without checking food safety rules. See the food safety guidance in this knowledge bank.
evidence: PMFME PIB releases read. FSSAI rules were not read here.
verify_with: District Food Safety Officer / FSSAI helpline

question_en: How do I put my homestay on Google Maps so guests can find me?
answer: Use Google Business Profile. It is free. You add your place, then Google verifies you by phone or SMS, email, video call or postcard, depending on what is offered. Review can take up to 5 business days. Add true photos, correct location, phone number and clear rules.
actions: Create a profile on business.google.com with the exact name and place.
Verify with the method Google gives you.
Add real photos, contact number and booking rules, and reply to reviews.
caution: Do not put wrong or fake details. Never share your bank PIN or OTP with 'Google support' callers.
evidence: Google Business Profile help page read 2 Oct 2026.

question_en: How can I use WhatsApp Business for bookings?
answer: WhatsApp Business is a free-to-download app. You can make a catalogue of rooms, meals or experiences, set quick replies for common questions, use labels for new, confirmed and paid guests, and set greeting and away messages. Use one number for business only.
actions: Install the WhatsApp Business app on a phone used for work.
Create catalogue items with photo, short text and policy.
Set quick replies for check-in time, directions, payment and cancellation.
caution: Do not send guests' Aadhaar or ID photos in public groups. Share only what is needed.
evidence: WhatsApp Business page read 2 Oct 2026.

question_en: How do I take UPI payments from guests safely?
answer: Put a printed QR code of your bank account or business account at the desk. When a guest pays, check the credit in your own bank app or SMS before you hand over goods. Never enter your UPI PIN to receive money. Keep a payment note with date, amount and guest name.
actions: Get a QR code from your bank or UPI app in the name of your business.
Check each credit in your bank app, not only on the guest's screen.
Keep daily payment totals in your cash book.
caution: If anyone asks you to enter a PIN to receive money, it is a fraud. Call 1930 if you lose money.
evidence: Fraud helpline 1930 from PIB release. NPCI pages could not be read. Method is general practice.

question_en: What should our booking and cancellation policy say?
answer: Write a short policy in simple words and send it before you accept an advance. Include: what the advance is, last date for free cancellation, what you refund and when, what happens if you cancel for weather or safety, and what happens if guests arrive late or leave early. Keep the same rule for everyone.
actions: Write the rule in 5 to 6 lines in English and your local language.
Send it by WhatsApp before taking an advance.
Keep proof of the guest's reply.
caution: Consumer law may apply to refunds. Ask your District Consumer office if unsure.
evidence: Practice-based method. No percentages given.

question_en: Someone I do not know wants to book and send me money, and asks me to send some back. Is it a scam?
answer: Yes, it may be a scam. Common tricks: send a QR code and ask you to scan to 'receive' money, overpay and ask for a refund, or send a fake payment screenshot. Never scan a QR or enter a PIN to receive money. Confirm the credit in your own bank app. Do not refund before the money is in your account.
actions: Stop talking and do not send money back.
Report at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930 if you lost money.
Tell your bank immediately.
caution: Report quickly. Keep chat and payment records.
evidence: PIB release on cyber frauds: 1930 and cybercrime.gov.in.

question_en: Should I list my homestay on online travel sites?
answer: Online platforms can bring guests but take a commission. Read the terms on cancellation, payments, guest reviews and taxes before you list. Start with one platform, keep your rate and availability up to date, and keep direct bookings through WhatsApp and Google too.
actions: Compare two platforms on commission, payout time and cancellation rules.
Use true photos and clear house rules.
Block dates in all places when you get a booking.
caution: Platform rules and commission can change. You may need GST or other registrations. Ask a tax adviser.
evidence: Practice-based. No platform terms read.

question_en: A tour operator wants to send guests to us. How do I deal with them?
answer: A tour operator or DMC often buys your service at a net rate and adds its own margin, or takes a commission. Ask for a written agreement. It should say rooms, meals, dates, group size, rates, advance, payment time, cancellation and who is responsible for guest safety. Keep the final say on cultural rules and photography.
actions: Ask the operator for a written booking confirmation for each group.
Agree the payment date and the cancellation terms before the group arrives.
Share your village's visitor rules with the operator.
caution: Do not give goods or services on credit without a written agreement.
evidence: Practice-based method. No commission numbers.

question_en: Can we post guests' photos or village people's photos on social media?
answer: Always ask first. Take permission from each adult before you photograph or post them. Take extra care with children, women and sacred or private places. For guests, ask before posting their faces. Keep a simple consent line or message. If someone says no, do not post.
actions: Ask for consent in simple words before you photograph.
Do not post photos of children without a parent's clear consent.
Remove a photo quickly if someone asks.
caution: Data protection rules may apply. Ask the law agent in this knowledge bank.
evidence: Practice-based.

question_en: A guest wrote a bad review. What should I do?
answer: Reply politely and quickly, in a calm voice. Thank the guest, say sorry for the problem, say what you will fix, and offer to talk offline. Do not argue or reveal private details. Fix real problems and tell your team. Keep a complaints register.
actions: Write a short reply the same day or next day.
Fix the problem and note it in your register.
Ask satisfied guests to share honest reviews.
caution: Do not write fake reviews or pay for good reviews.
evidence: Practice-based. Google profile page was read for the profile steps only.

question_en: Do I need to take guests' Aadhaar or ID? How do I keep it safe?
answer: Rules for guest registers and ID, especially for foreign guests, are set by state law and police. Ask your local police station or District Tourism Office what your state needs. Collect only what the rule requires. Do not post ID photos in WhatsApp groups. Keep paper registers in a locked place.
actions: Ask the District Tourism Office and police what registration is needed.
Keep ID copies only as long as required and store them safely.
Never share Aadhaar numbers on social media.
caution: See the legal and compliance guidance in this knowledge bank for the exact rules.
evidence: Pointer only. No rule read.
verify_with: Local police / District Tourism Office / legal agent

question_en: How can all families benefit, not just the ones with the biggest house?
answer: Three methods are used: (1) rotate guest bookings among homestay families so each gets a turn; (2) add a small per-guest village fee for a shared fund, for example for school, water or repairs; (3) give income to other households through jobs like cooking, guiding, farm visits, craft sales or transport. Decide the method in a village meeting and write it down.
actions: List the services guests need and the households who can provide them.
Choose a rotation list and keep it visible.
Agree what the village fund will pay for and report it every season.
caution: Rotation can lower quality if some homes are not ready. Combine with minimum standards. Do not copy numbers from other villages.
evidence: Practice-based method.

question_en: I hire a cook and a helper in peak season. What wages must I pay?
answer: The four Labour Codes came into force on 21 November 2025. They give workers a statutory right to minimum wages and timely payment. They also require appointment letters. The wage rate depends on your state and type of work, so ask your state Labour Department or the Labour Commissioner. Pay on the agreed date.
actions: Ask the Labour Department or Labour Commissioner office for the current minimum wage for your type of work.
Give each worker a short written appointment letter with pay and date of payment.
Pay by bank or UPI and keep a register.
caution: Old state rules continue until new rules are notified, as far as they match the Codes. This is not legal advice.
evidence: PIB release (Feb 2026) on Labour Codes. Wage rates not read.

topic: Written agreement with guides and cooks
question_en: Do I need a written agreement with a local guide or cook?
answer: A short written agreement avoids fights. For employees, the Labour Codes say they should get an appointment letter. For freelance guides or cooks, write: what work, which days, how much for each guest or day, when payment is made, who pays for food and travel, cancellation, and who takes responsibility if a guest is hurt.
actions: Write the terms on one page and read it aloud together.
Both sign and each keep a copy.
Pay on the date agreed.
caution: Whether the person is a worker or an independent guide depends on the law. Ask the Labour Department or a lawyer.
evidence: PIB release states appointment letters under Labour Codes. Agreement content is general practice.

question_en: How can women, youth and elders all take part in tourism and get paid fairly?
answer: Give each group real paid roles. Women can run kitchens, craft sales and homestays and hold leadership roles. Youth can handle phones, bookings, photography and guiding. Elders can tell stories, teach crafts and songs, and should be paid for their time and knowledge. Agree the payment in advance and record it.
actions: Hold a meeting with women, youth and elders to ask what roles they want.
List roles with pay and training needs.
Make sure at least one woman and one youth sit on the decision group.
caution: Do not ask elders or women to perform for free. Do not share sacred or private knowledge without community permission.
evidence: Practice-based.

question_en: Tourism is only good for a few months. How do we manage the rest of the year?
answer: Do not depend only on tourism. Keep farming, livestock and crafts going. Save part of the peak season income in a group reserve. Use lean months for training, repairs, product making and planning. Offer small local experiences all year, such as farm tasks or cooking, if guests are available.
actions: List your income by month and mark lean months.
Set aside a portion of season income in a reserve account.
Plan repairs and training in lean months.
caution: A loan repayment due in lean months can be risky.
evidence: Practice-based.

question_en: We are farmers. What do we need to be ready to host guests on the farm?
answer: The Ministry of Tourism says state governments lead tourism development, so rules and help differ by state. Start small. Make a crop calendar so you know what guests can see or do in each month. Keep the farm safe for visitors: fence ponds, store chemicals, keep animals under control. Treat tourism as extra income, not a replacement for farming.
actions: Draw a month-by-month crop and activity calendar.
Check safety around ponds, machines and chemicals.
Ask your KVK and State Tourism Department what support exists in your state.
caution: Insurance, licences and farm-stay rules vary by state. Ask your District Tourism Office.
evidence: PIB rural tourism release and ICAR KVK page. Safety checklist is general practice.

question_en: Can I sell vegetables, honey or ghee directly to guests?
answer: Fresh produce sold to guests is direct sale and often simple. Processed or packed foods like honey, ghee, jam and pickle are food products and need food safety rules such as FSSAI registration or licence. PMFME may support food processing. Ask your food safety officer about your product.
actions: List products you can sell now without processing.
Ask the food safety officer about registration for processed items.
Use clean packing with a label and date.
caution: See the food safety guidance in this knowledge bank.
evidence: PMFME PIB release read. Food law not read.

question_en: How can our FPO help with selling to tourism or value-added products?
answer: FPOs can help farmers aggregate produce, process it, and sell together. The central FPO scheme gives support such as management cost and equity grants, but amounts quoted by PIB may have changed. Your FPO can supply hotels, homestays and shops with regular produce. Check the objects in your FPO papers first.
actions: Ask your FPO's CEO or promoter what products it can supply regularly.
Offer homestays a simple product list with prices and delivery days.
Agree payment terms in writing.
caution: FPO funds must follow FPO rules.
evidence: PIB release on FPOs read.
verify_with: FPO promoting agency / District Agriculture Office

question_en: Who do I meet first in the district to get help with loans, training or registration?
answer: Start with the people close to you. DAY-NRLM Block Mission Manager for SHG and livelihood help. District Industries Centre (DIC) for Udyam, PMEGP and MSME schemes. Lead District Manager (LDM) of the lead bank for loans. District Tourism Office for homestay registration and tourism schemes. Krishi Vigyan Kendra for farm skills. Common Service Centre for online forms. A local NGO can help you plan and facilitate.
actions: Write your goal in one line.
Visit the best matching office with your Aadhaar, PAN and a one-page plan.
Ask for names and phone numbers of the officer and write them down.
caution: Offices and names differ by state. Do not pay agents for free services.
evidence: Roles drawn from the PIB DAY-NRLM release and ICAR KVK page. Other offices are general practice.
